newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybeans end mixed in slow trading.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybeans end mixed in slow trading.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mixed in slow trading on Tuesday on a lack of market-moving news after rises on Monday, traders said.
The most active November contract fell seven yuan per tonne to 3,352 yuan ($404) per tonne. It opened at 3,350, hitting an intraday high of 3,355 and a low of 3,348.
March rose 20 to 3,100, May was up 67 to 3,167, July fell 69 to 3,271, September was unchanged at 3,350 and the January 1998 contract fell four to 3,348.
Combined volume rose to 18,500 tonnes from 17,700.
Traders said the market attracted few investors because there was no market-moving news.
"Most investors traded for quick profits, which prevented soybeans from making any further rises," one trader said.
"This is the situation that is likely to prevail in the short term with trading dominated by retail investors," he said.
Some traders said they expected soybeans to rise further once fundamentals improved.
